taste.name: Let the image be the card
taste.trigger: When designing a tile for content that is itself visual
taste.decision: Chose a bare image with a 16px radius over a framed card with border, background, padding and drop shadow
taste.reason: Because people scan by eye and every frame line is noise multiplied across dozens of tiles
evidence: only 2 shadows on page, both on floating UI

taste.name: Keep the image's own height (masonry)
taste.trigger: When displaying images of mixed aspect ratios side by side
taste.decision: Chose fixed column width with free height over a uniform-ratio grid with cropping
taste.reason: Because cropping changes what people came to see, and staggered edges stop the page reading like a spreadsheet

taste.name: Red only for verbs
taste.trigger: When the brand owns a loud red
taste.decision: Chose to keep #E60023 off headings, links, borders and backgrounds, reserving it for primary actions, over spreading the brand colour across the chrome
taste.reason: Because the imagery already competes for attention, so the one saturated UI colour has to mean 'do this'

taste.name: One typeface, contrast through weight
taste.trigger: When type must sit next to busy, colourful imagery
taste.decision: Chose a single sans in four weights over a display + body pairing
taste.reason: Because a characterful display face would fight the photos; big weight jumps give hierarchy without adding a second voice
